chest.nutrition_focus: Chest day is typically a heavier pushing session — have a carb-and-protein meal (oatmeal and eggs, or chicken and rice) about 1-2 hours before training for energy, then get a fast-absorbing protein source (a shake or lean meat) in within 2 hours after to support muscle repair.

exercises.name: Barbell Bench Press
steps: Lie flat on the bench with your feet planted firmly on the floor.
Grip the barbell slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Unrack the bar and stabilize it directly over your chest with locked elbows.
Lower the bar slowly and under control until it lightly touches your mid-chest.
Push the bar back up explosively by driving your back into the bench and extending your arms.
posture: Keep a slight, natural arch in your lower back; do not lift your glutes off the bench.
Retract and depress your shoulder blades into the bench to protect your shoulders.
Keep your wrists stacked directly over your elbows; do not let your wrists bend backward.
Tuck your elbows to roughly 45 to 75 degrees rather than flaring to 90, to protect your rotator cuffs.
common_mistakes: Bouncing the barbell off the chest to gain momentum.
Lifting the hips and glutes off the bench to force a heavy weight up.
Allowing the bar to drop too quickly without controlling the eccentric phase.
exercises.rep_guidance: For muscle growth, 3 to 4 sets of 8 to 12 reps with 2 minutes of rest. For raw strength, 4 to 5 sets of 3 to 5 reps with 3 minutes of rest.

exercises.name: Push-Up
steps: Start in a high plank position with hands slightly wider than shoulder-width apart.
Keep your body in a straight line from head to heels, engaging your core and glutes.
Lower your chest toward the floor by bending your elbows to roughly 45 degrees from your torso.
Push back up to the starting position by extending your arms fully.
posture: Keep your neck neutral, looking slightly ahead of your hands rather than straight down.
Don't let your hips sag or pike up — keep a rigid plank throughout.
Keep your shoulder blades stable; avoid letting them wing out at the top.
common_mistakes: Flaring the elbows out to a full 90 degrees, which stresses the shoulders.
Only doing a partial range of motion instead of lowering the chest close to the floor.
Letting the hips drop first instead of moving the whole body as one unit.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 to 4 sets to near failure (often 8 to 20 reps) works well. Add weight on your back once bodyweight reps exceed 20.

back.nutrition_focus: Back day tends to be volume-heavy with a lot of pulling and grip work — stay well hydrated, and lean on complex carbs before training with a solid protein source (chicken, fish, or a shake) afterward to support recovery of the large back musculature.

exercises.name: Conventional Barbell Deadlift
exercises.target_muscle: Hamstrings, Glutes, Entire Back (Erectors, Lats), Core
steps: Stand with your feet hip-width apart, with the barbell cutting directly across the middle of your feet.
Hinge at your hips and bend your knees slightly to grip the bar just outside your legs.
Flatten your back completely, pull your chest up, and drop your hips until your shins touch the bar.
Drive your feet hard into the floor, pulling the bar up in a straight vertical line close to your body.
Lock out your hips and knees fully at the top, then reverse the movement under control.
posture: Your back must stay flat like a tabletop; zero rounding in the lumbar or thoracic spine.
Keep your shoulders set slightly in front of the bar before you lift.
Engage your lats completely by imagining you're trying to crush oranges in your armpits.
common_mistakes: Rounding the lower back under heavy loads, which risks serious spinal injury.
Starting with the barbell too far forward away from the shins, killing your leverage.
Hyperextending and leaning backward excessively at the top lockout.
exercises.rep_guidance: Because the deadlift heavily taxes your nervous system, keep volume lower: 3 sets of 5 reps, or 1 to 2 heavy sets of 5, is optimal.

exercises.name: Bent-Over Barbell Row
steps: Stand with feet shoulder-width apart, gripping the barbell just outside your knees.
Hinge at your hips until your torso is roughly 45 degrees to the floor, with a soft bend in the knees.
Let the bar hang at arm's length below your shoulders, then pull it up toward your lower ribcage.
Squeeze your shoulder blades together at the top, then lower the bar back down under control.
posture: Keep your back flat throughout — no rounding of the lumbar spine while the bar is loaded.
Keep your core braced to support your spine in the hinged position.
Pull with your elbows, not your hands — drive your elbows toward the ceiling.
common_mistakes: Standing too upright, turning the row into a shrug instead of a back exercise.
Using momentum by jerking the torso up to heave the weight.
Rounding the lower back under load.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 to 4 sets of 8 to 12 reps for muscle growth, resting 90 seconds to 2 minutes between sets.

biceps.nutrition_focus: Arm days like biceps carry lower overall training volume and energy demand than compound days, so a moderate pre-workout snack is enough — the priority is steady protein intake through the day rather than a big pre-workout meal.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Bicep Curl
steps: Stand tall with a dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging extended at your sides, palms facing forward.
Keeping your upper arms pinned to your torso, exhale and squeeze your biceps to curl the weights upward.
Continue raising the dumbbells until your biceps are fully contracted at shoulder level.
Inhale and slowly lower the dumbbells back down with absolute control.
posture: Keep your elbows locked into your sides; do not let them drift forward or swing out.
Stand completely still with a braced core; do not use your hips to swing the weights up.
Maintain a straight neck and relaxed shoulders; do not shrug the weight up with your traps.
common_mistakes: Swinging the torso back and forth to cheat the weight up through momentum.
Failing to extend the arms completely at the bottom, robbing the bicep of a full stretch.
Letting the elbows flare out wide, which recruits the front shoulders instead of the biceps.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 sets of 10 to 15 controlled reps, focusing on time under tension.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Hammer Curl
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand with a neutral grip, palms facing your torso.
Keeping your elbows pinned to your sides, curl the weights up toward your shoulders.
Squeeze at the top without rotating your wrists — the neutral grip stays neutral throughout.
Lower the dumbbells back down slowly and under control.
posture: Keep your elbows locked at your sides the entire rep; don't let them drift forward.
Avoid swinging your torso to generate momentum.
Keep your wrists straight and neutral, not bent backward or forward.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight and turning the movement into a shoulder swing.
Letting the elbows drift forward, which shifts tension off the biceps.
Not fully extending the arms at the bottom of each rep.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 sets of 10 to 15 reps, prioritizing a controlled tempo over heavy weight.

triceps.nutrition_focus: Like biceps, triceps work is isolation-focused with lower overall energy demand — focus on consistent protein throughout the day, and a light carb source (fruit, rice cakes) beforehand is plenty since you're not moving heavy compound loads.

exercises.name: Cable Tricep Pushdown
exercises.equipment: Cable Machine, Straight or Rope Attachment
steps: Stand facing a high cable pulley with a bar or rope attachment, elbows tucked at your sides.
Starting with forearms parallel to the floor, push the attachment down by extending your elbows.
Fully extend your arms at the bottom, squeezing your triceps hard.
Slowly return to the starting position under control, keeping your elbows fixed.
posture: Keep your elbows pinned to your ribcage throughout — they shouldn't move forward or backward.
Keep a slight forward lean from the hips, not the lower back, to stabilize the movement.
Avoid leaning your whole bodyweight into the movement to push more weight.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows flare out or drift away from the body, reducing tricep isolation.
Using body momentum instead of just the arms.
Not fully extending at the bottom, cutting the range of motion short.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 sets of 10 to 15 reps works well for building tricep size and endurance.

exercises.name: Overhead Dumbbell Tricep Extension
steps: Sit or stand holding one dumbbell with both hands, arms extended straight overhead.
Keeping your upper arms close to your head, bend your elbows to lower the dumbbell behind your head.
Lower until your forearms are roughly parallel to the floor, feeling a stretch in the triceps.
Extend your elbows to press the dumbbell back to the starting overhead position.
posture: Keep your upper arms stationary and close to your ears throughout the movement.
Brace your core to avoid arching your lower back as the weight moves behind your head.
Keep your elbows pointed forward, not flared out to the sides.
common_mistakes: Letting the elbows flare outward, reducing triceps tension and stressing the shoulders.
Using too heavy a weight and losing control on the way down.
Arching the lower back to compensate instead of keeping the core braced.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 sets of 10 to 12 reps, using a lighter weight than you'd expect — this is a stretched, vulnerable position for the joint.

shoulders.nutrition_focus: Shoulder day involves smaller, more injury-prone joints under load — a light-to-moderate pre-workout meal is fine, and post-workout protein remains the priority. Staying hydrated also helps joint mobility during pressing and raising movements.

exercises.name: Barbell Overhead Press (Military Press)
exercises.target_muscle: Front and Side Deltoids, Triceps, Upper Chest, Core
steps: Set the barbell at upper chest height, grip it just outside shoulder-width, and unrack it across your front shoulders.
Step back, squeeze your glutes, brace your abs tight, and pull your chin back slightly.
Press the bar directly overhead in a straight vertical line, moving your face out of the way as it passes.
Punch your head forward through your arms at the top lockout position to stabilize the load.
Lower the barbell under control back down to your front collarbone area.
posture: Keep your glutes and core fully squeezed; this prevents dangerous over-arching of the lower back.
Your forearms must remain vertical and directly underneath the barbell throughout the bottom half.
Lock your knees completely straight; don't bend them to use leg drive.
common_mistakes: Leaning backward excessively from the waist, turning it into an accidental incline press.
Failing to lock out the elbows fully at the top of the movement.
Bumping the bar against the chin or nose because the head path isn't cleared.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 to 4 sets of 6 to 8 reps for a balance of shoulder mass and pressing power.

exercises.name: Dumbbell Lateral Raise
steps: Stand tall holding a dumbbell in each hand at your sides, palms facing your torso.
With a slight bend in your elbows, raise both arms out to the sides until shoulder height.
Pause briefly at the top, keeping your wrists level with or slightly below your elbows.
Lower the dumbbells back down slowly and under control.
posture: Keep a slight, fixed bend in your elbows throughout — don't lock them straight.
Avoid shrugging your shoulders up toward your ears as you raise the weight.
Keep your torso still; don't use momentum by swinging or leaning.
common_mistakes: Using too much weight, which forces the traps to take over instead of the side delts.
Raising the arms above shoulder height, shifting stress onto the shoulder joint.
Swinging the weight up using body momentum instead of controlled deltoid strength.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 sets of 12 to 15 reps with a light-to-moderate weight, prioritizing strict form over load.

legs.nutrition_focus: Leg day burns the most energy of any session — this is the day to prioritize carbohydrates both before (for fuel) and after (to replenish glycogen), alongside a solid protein source, since leg training recruits the most total muscle mass.

exercises.name: Barbell Back Squat
steps: Set the barbell just below shoulder height and step under it, placing it across your upper back.
Unrack the bar, take two steps back, and set your feet shoulder-width apart with toes slightly flared.
Take a deep breath into your stomach, brace your core, and begin by hinging your hips back.
Lower your body until your thighs are at least parallel to the floor, keeping your chest proud.
Drive through your mid-foot to stand back up, exhaling as you clear the hardest part of the lift.
posture: Maintain a neutral spine throughout the entire lift; don't let your lower back round at the bottom.
Keep your chest upright and head facing forward or slightly down to preserve neck alignment.
Ensure your knees track in a straight line with your toes; don't let them cave inward.
common_mistakes: Not squatting deep enough (stopping well short of parallel thighs).
Allowing the heels to lift off the floor, shifting dangerous load onto the knee joints.
Letting the knees collapse inward when pushing out of the bottom position.
exercises.rep_guidance: For general size, 3 to 4 sets of 8 to 12 reps. For strength, 4 to 5 sets of 5 reps.

exercises.name: Leg Press
steps: Sit in the leg press machine with your back flat against the pad and feet shoulder-width apart on the platform.
Release the safety catches and lower the platform by bending your knees toward your chest.
Lower until your knees reach about a 90-degree angle, keeping your lower back pressed into the pad.
Push through your heels to extend your legs back to the starting position, without locking your knees out hard.
posture: Keep your lower back flat against the pad throughout — don't let your hips round up off the seat.
Keep your knees tracking in line with your toes; don't let them cave inward.
Avoid locking your knees out completely and aggressively at the top of each rep.
common_mistakes: Lowering the platform too far, causing the lower back to round off the pad.
Placing feet too high or too low on the platform, shifting stress unevenly onto knees or hips.
Locking the knees out hard at the top, stressing the joint.
exercises.rep_guidance: 3 to 4 sets of 10 to 15 reps — pairs well with squats as a lower-fatigue way to add extra leg volume.

rest.nutrition_focus: On your rest day, keep protein intake steady to support ongoing muscle repair, but ease off on the extra training-day carbohydrates since you're not burning through glycogen with a workout — focus on whole foods, vegetables, and hydration.
